profile.driver: scripts/benchmark-index.ps1 (actual src/index.rs snapshot + production locale comparator; UI/provider branches unused)
profile.original: unmodified original file-index-worker.js + native/file-indexer.exe in Electron 38.1.2, Node 22.19.0, ICU 74.2, Unicode 15.1

fixture.storage: task-only synthetic files on C drive; no user files
fixture.scanBoundary: Rust Index::start until building=false; original configure request until building=false, polled every 10ms. File fixture creation excluded. SQLite cold database, OS cache not reset.
fixture.queries: 100 measured worker round trips alternating needle and *needle*, limit 40; Rust discards 10 warmup iterations; original query cases run before timing

notes: Before is the Rust correctness-compatible implementation before prepared statement/frequency/metadata/cold-insert optimization. Its cached unicode-normalization dependency was 0.1.26; final after runs use pinned 0.1.23 / Unicode 15.1. The fixed performance corpus predates outlined Unicode16 characters and contains no normalization mappings changed by that pin.

The first final after run overlapped cargo compilation; the repeat did not deliberately run a concurrent build. Measurements are individual local samples, not statistically controlled cross-machine results.
Final Rust query latency is close to the original Electron implementation; scan latency varies around the original. These results do not show the complete Rust application is faster.
Correctness separately validated with 553 original entries / 55 queries plus real scan Unicode16, combining marks, exclusions, watches and migration tests.

Integer-ID samples use the final explicit INTEGER PRIMARY KEY schema. Hidden rowids are migrated atomically before compaction so VACUUM cannot invalidate token references. 10,031-row database: 13,606,912 bytes, versus 78,864,384 for the preceding Rust path-token schema and 11,255,808 for the original.

Two final Rust samples scan in 566.42 / 693.77 ms; a same-day original sample takes 2233.85 ms. These are local warm-OS-cache samples, not a controlled benchmark. Query latency includes worker round trip; direct queries use a fresh frequency map and are reported separately.
